entities.summary:
Bonaventura Badoardo de Peraga (1332-06-30, Padua – 1389-06-18, Rome) was a prominent Italian Augustinian friar, theologian, and cardinal whose career unfolded amidst the profound ecclesiastical and political turmoil of the late 14th century, most notably the Western Schism. Born into a noble family in Padua, he rose through the Augustinian Order, becoming a respected scholar and administrator, ultimately playing a role in the papal controversies that divided Europe. His life exemplifies the challenges faced by religious leaders navigating a fractured Christendom and the complex interplay between spiritual authority and temporal power during the Medieval era.

After completing his theological studies, Bonaventura taught at various Augustinian studia before earning his doctorate from the University of Paris. He was elected Prior General of the Augustinian Order in 1377, a position he held for two terms, overseeing the order's administration and intellectual life. Initially a supporter of Pope Urban VI following the disputed papal election of 1378, he later shifted his allegiance to the Avignonese Pope Clement VII, who elevated him to cardinal in 1381. This transition reflected the deep divisions within the Church, as Bonaventura moved from Rome to Avignon, becoming a key figure in Clement VII's curia and participating in efforts to consolidate the Avignonese claim to the papacy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bonaventura Badoardo de Peraga's rise to cardinal under Clement VII directly contributed to the entrenchment of the Western Schism, influencing the political and religious landscape of late Medieval Europe. His administrative leadership within the Augustinian Order also demonstrated resilience amidst widespread ecclesiastical fragmentation.
